question: How do the USDA's August 2025 revisions to soybean acreage and production, combined with the subsequent volatility in Wholesale Boxed Beef pricing during the Labor Day run, impact the projected Q3 operating margins for U.S.-based livestock and feed processors?
report:
# USDA's August 2025 Soybean Revisions and the Labor Day Boxed Beef Spike: Read‑Through to Q3 Operating Margins for U.S. Livestock and Feed Processors

**Evidence cutoff: 2025-09-02 (inclusive). Facts below are drawn only from documents published on or before that date.**

## Direct answer

The two shocks are **not symmetric in magnitude, and they do not hit the same cost line**. The USDA's 12 August 2025 revisions cut soybean acreage and production (a mildly *inflationary* signal for meal-based feed costs), while the boxed beef cutout's surge above $400/cwt into Labor Day was a far larger, but *mixed*, event: it raised revenue per pound while fed cattle costs sat at records, so it improved **gross spreads without by itself restoring positive packer margins**. On pre-cutoff evidence, the most defensible projection for **calendar Q3 2025** is: (i) **beef packers narrow but do not close losses** (cash margin estimates were still **‑$181.50/head in late July**; the August cutout gain is worth roughly **$234–469/head of carcass value** if it sticks); (ii) **branded/value-added processors stay under pressure** — Hormel cut FY25 adjusted EPS guidance on 28 Aug, blaming "the steep rise in commodity input costs"; (iii) **feed-dependent poultry and hog integrators get modest relief**, because the soybean revision was largely swamped by a record corn crop and meal prices still **below $300/ton**. Protein-processing margins in Q3 should read as *better than Q2 but still well below the branded-food benchmark*: roughly **3–4% adjusted operating margin for multi-protein integrators versus ~8% for branded processors** (Tyson 3.6% adjusted vs Hormel 8.4% in the latest reported quarters).

## Fact base

**1. USDA August revisions (published 12 Aug 2025).** NASS cut soybean **planted acreage from 83.4 to 80.9 million acres** while raising corn from 95.2 to 97.3 million ([farmdoc daily, 18 Aug](https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/2025/08/yes-there-are-a-lot-of-corn-acres-evidence-from-fsa-acreage-data.html)). WASDE-663 projected soybean **harvested area of 80.1 million acres (‑2.4 million m/m)** on a **record 53.6 bu/ac (+1.1)**, giving 2025/26 production of **~4.3 billion bushels, ‑43 million vs July and ‑290 million vs last year's 4.36 billion**; beginning stocks ‑20 million bu, exports ‑40 million bu to 1.7 billion, crush unchanged at 2.54 billion, **ending stocks 290 million bu (‑20 m/m; 6.3% stocks/use)** at an unchanged $10.10/bu season-average price ([American Farm Bureau, 12 Aug](https://www.fb.org/intel/markets/wasde-robust-crops-high-input-costs-strained-margins)). The market read was bullish-soybeans/bearish-corn: **November soybeans closed +21¢ at $10.32** while **December corn fell 13¢ to $3.94**, the first sub-$4 close for a 2025 corn contract, with corn output raised to a **record 16.7 billion bu** and ending stocks of 2.1 billion bu, the highest since 2018/19 (same source). Soybean production was "at the low end of pre-report estimates," with world ending stocks trimmed 1.17 MMT to 124.9 MMT ([Grain Farmers of Ontario, 18 Aug](https://gfo.ca/market-trends/market-trends-report-august-september-2025)).

**2. Boxed beef, Labor Day run.** The USDA Choice 600–900 lb cutout was **$400.57/cwt for the week ending 15 Aug (+$21.73 w/w, +$27.02 m/m, +26.2% y/y vs $317.45; 5-year average $289.06)**; Select was $370.76, the Choice/Select spread widened $6.06 to $29.81, and the CME Feeder Cattle Index reached **345.75 (52-week high 346.01 on 13 Aug; 322.28 a month earlier; 246.71 a year earlier)** ([Cattle Range Weekly Market Summary, 15 Aug](https://cattlerange.com/static/assets/3gdp4btx/wms_08-15-25m.pdf)). LMIC confirms the holiday mechanism: the cutout "turned higher the first week of August and reached above $400 per cwt by the end of the month, **largely driven by demand leading up to the Labor Day Holiday**. The last time the boxed beef cutout value topped $400 per cwt was late May 2020" ([LMIC Margins and Markets, Aug 2025](https://lmic.info/wp-content/lmic-files/lmic-data/tac/publications/Margins%20and%20Markets/2025/Margins%20and%20Markets%2008-27-25.pdf)). Trade commentary put August's monthly gain at **+$54.09, higher in 17 of 21 sessions — "the best August in history"** ([National Beef Wire, 1 Sep](https://www.facebook.com/NationalBeefWireDVAuction/posts/1520663878905007)).

**3. Where margins stood entering Q3.** Sterling Marketing had **packer margins at ‑$181.50/head** in the post-July-4 week (from ‑$208.72 a month earlier), a comprehensive beef cutout averaging $376.86, slaughter of 563,000 head/wk, **867 lb carcasses**, 79.0% cutout utilization, and a **full-year projection of ‑$205/head** ([Meatingplace, 28 Jul](https://meatingplace.com/beef-packers-face-an-unprofitable-2025)). Structural supply, per LMIC: **July 1 cattle inventory 94.2 million head, the lowest in the report's history**; Aug 1 feedlot inventory **10.9 million (‑1.6% y/y)** with July marketings **‑5.7%** and placements **‑6.1%**; the Mexico cattle border closed for New World Screwworm; **H1 beef imports +33% to 2.9 billion lb**, exports ‑8%; **all-fresh retail beef $8.90/lb in July, a record, +9% y/y**.

**4. Company-reported margins (both pre-cutoff).** Tyson (FY25 Q3 ended 31 May, reported **4 Aug**): sales $13.884 bn (+4.0%), **GAAP operating margin 1.9%, adjusted 3.6%**, adjusted EPS $0.91, a **$343 million Beef goodwill impairment**, FY25 adjusted operating income **$2.1–2.3 bn** with **Beef adjusted loss $(475)–$(375) million**, Pork $175–200 million, Chicken $1.3–1.4 bn, Prepared $925 million–$1.0 bn ([Tyson, 4 Aug](https://www.tysonfoods.com/news/news-releases/2025/8/tyson-foods-reports-third-quarter-2025-results)). Hormel (Q3 FY25 ended 27 Jul, reported **28 Aug**): sales $3.03 bn (+6% organic), **operating margin 7.9%, adjusted 8.4%**, segment profit ‑4% Retail / ‑1% Foodservice / ‑13% International, FY25 adjusted EPS guidance **cut to $1.43–$1.45 from $1.58–$1.68**, and Q4 (Aug–Oct) adjusted EPS **$0.38–$0.40** with "near-term pressures … persisting through the fourth quarter" ([Hormel, 28 Aug](https://www.hormelfoods.com/newsroom/press-releases/hormel-foods-reports-third-quarter-fiscal-2025-results)).

## Mechanisms (inference)

**(a) Beef: a value spike, not a margin gift.** The cutout is a wholesale *value* index, not a spread. At 867 lb carcass weight, the month-over-month cutout rise of $27.02/cwt equates to **≈$234/head of added carcass value**, and the whole August move (+$54.09) to **≈$469/head** — the same order of magnitude as the ‑$205/head full-year loss projection. Against that, feeder and fed cattle prices were rising simultaneously (CME Feeder Index +7.3% m/m; the $113/cwt y/y cutout gain coincided with a $99 y/y feeder-index gain), so **the realized Q3 improvement is the difference of two rallies**. LMIC's read is that strength "is likely a signal that fed cattle prices will be supported" — i.e. packers pay much of it back at the scale.

**(b) Feed: second-order.** Using published finishing-ratio sensitivities (**each $0.10/bu corn ≈ $0.43/cwt feed cost; each $10/ton meal ≈ $0.37/cwt**; [farmdoc daily, 6 Dec 2024](https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/2024/12/prospects-for-swine-feed-costs-in-2025.html)), a $10/ton meal move is **~0.4% of a ~$170/cwt hog cost basis**. A 1% production cut (‑43 million of 4.3 billion bushels) and 6.3% stocks/use are therefore small next to the **record corn crop**. LMIC's own feed picture is supportive: corn "flirt[ing] with $4/bushel," **meal and hay below $300 and $200/ton**, and **July farrow-to-finish returns of $51.90/head (best since June 2021) on total feed cost of $86.25/head (‑7% y/y, meal ‑25%)**. The relevant feed-processor risk is **crush**, not feed cost: meal was already weak enough that "low meal prices pose risks to soybean crush margins," with SOYBEX FOB Santos at $449.58/mt (+12% y/y) on 22 Aug ([S&P Global, 26 Aug](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/agriculture/082625-low-meal-prices-pose-risks-to-soybean-crush-margins-in-south-america)); the acreage cut firms beans and meal, but USDA's ‑40 million bu export revision and unchanged 2.54 billion bu crush keep net crush economics thin for integrators that own the crush.

## Counterarguments and scenarios

*Counter to the bullish read:* the spike is **calendar-driven and reversible**, with wholesale values historically reaching a pre-Labor Day zenith followed by restocking support only; **record $8.90/lb retail beef** invites substitution (LMIC notes high beef and pork prices are pushing consumers to chicken at $2.43–2.48/lb); **imports +33%** and heavier carcasses blunt scarcity; and an independent crop-condition model using 11 Aug ratings estimated 4.2–4.4 billion bu, i.e. the production cut could unwind ([AgManager, 16 Aug](https://agmanager.info/sites/default/files/pdf/SoybeanYield_Conditions_08-18-25.pdf)). Tyson's **$343 million Beef goodwill impairment** shows the segment's problem is asset-level, not one holiday week.

- **Base:** cutout mean-reverts toward $370–400 after the holiday; Q3 packer cash margins improve from ‑$181.50/head toward ‑$50 to +$50/head; Tyson holds FY25 Beef loss guidance within $(475)–$(375) million — ≈**2.1% of FY24 Beef sales**, i.e. a segment operating margin near **‑2%**; multi-protein adjusted operating margin ~**3.5–4%**, branded processors ~**8%** with commodity drag persisting into Q4.
- **Upside:** demand and trim/export strength holds the cutout above $410 into September while fed cattle plateau → positive packer spreads, Beef losses narrowing toward $(375) million, and chicken/pork helped by lower feed.
- **Downside:** post-holiday retracement plus record fed cattle ("brutal second half," Sterling's ‑$205/head), consumer resistance at record retail, tariff/trade shocks (exports already ‑8%), and a rebound to 4.3–4.4 billion bu of soybeans that lifts meal supply, hurting crush-dependent feed operators even as integrators' feed costs fall.

## Uncertainties and evidence gaps

"Q3" is defined inconsistently: **Tyson's fiscal Q4 (Jun 29–Aug 30) and Hormel's fiscal Q4 (Aug 3–Nov 2) — not their reported Q3s — overlap calendar Q3**, so the calendar-quarter statements above are **inference from monthly market data and issuer guidance, not reported results**. Commodity price series retrieved after the cutoff are retrospective vintages, so all beef and feed figures here come from dated documents; the 12 Aug WASDE/NASS values are as-published and unrevised pre-cutoff. **Coverage gaps:** the Finnhub skill returned **no company news for TSN/TYSON (15 Jul–2 Sep) and no insider transactions (1 Jul–2 Sep; 3 records excluded as post-cutoff)**, and OpenBB was not queried because livestock and boxed-beef prices are outside its documented endpoints. There is therefore **no admitted pre-cutoff evidence for National Beef/JBS, Cargill, ADM, Bunge or Darling**, and no daily cutout series for the exact 25 Aug–2 Sep holiday week (weekly and monthly averages used instead). No claim is made about actual reported Q3 results, which did not exist by 2025-09-02.

# Mali's Fiscal Demands, Executive Detentions and Barrick (GOLD): Discount Arithmetic and Loulo-Gounkoto Viability

*Point-in-time research as at 2025-04-28. All facts below are from sources published on or before that date. Calculations labelled "author's estimate" derive from those admitted inputs plus explicitly stated assumptions.*

## Direct answer

As of the cutoff, the $160 million Resolute Mining settlement and Barrick's negotiated $438 million payment are best read as **the price of re-entry into Mali's new fiscal regime rather than a one-time legal cost**. They will not, by themselves, move Barrick's valuation much: $438m is roughly 1% of Barrick's late-April 2025 equity value and about 0.9 years of Loulo-Gounkoto's attributable 2024 EBITDA (author's estimate). The valuation discount is driven by something else — the market's inability to underwrite Malian cash flows at face value because the rules, not the bill, changed (state stake up to 30–35%, royalties 6%→10.5%). Loulo-Gounkoto remains **physically and geologically viable** (578koz produced in 2024, 5.13 g/t Q4 grade, $828/oz cash costs), so it is economic at any plausible gold price; the open question is **what share of that margin Barrick keeps**. Critically, as of April 28 the deal had *not* been executed by Bamako: Barrick said on April 15 that Mali closed its national office, threatened expropriation and blocked the agreement it had accepted in February, so the discount was still widening, not closing.

## What the settlements cost, in evidence

**Resolute (November 2024).** Resolute agreed to pay $160m — $80m immediately, the balance in coming months — after CEO Terry Holohan and two staff were detained on November 8–9 while travelling to Bamako for negotiations; the executives were released (~November 20) under a memorandum of understanding requiring "all outstanding claims against the company in Mali to be settled" ([ABC News, 18 Nov 2024](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-11-18/resolute-mining-to-pay-mali-government-after-executives-detained/104614270); [CEOWORLD, 21 Nov 2024](https://ceoworld.biz/2024-11-21/resolute-mining-executives-released-in-mali-after-160-million-settlement); [Reuters, 19 Feb 2025](https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/barrick-gold-signs-agreement-with-mali-end-mining-dispute-2025-02-19)). Mali's position was that Resolute owed $161m identified in a sector-wide audit ([CEOWORLD](https://ceoworld.biz/2024-11-21/resolute-mining-executives-released-in-mali-after-160-million-settlement)). Resolute's Q4 report (30 Jan 2025) shows the cash hit (drawn overdraft of $34.2m) and — more importantly — quantifies the *recurring* burden: Syama's 2025 AISC guidance of $1,700–1,800/oz is inflated by "an additional ~$250/oz or around $175/oz at a Group level" purely from transitioning to the 2023 Mining Code ([Resolute activities report](https://www.rml.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025-01-250130-RSG-ASX-December-Quarterly-Report-FINAL.pdf)). At the guided ~202.5koz midpoint, $250/oz ≈ **$50.6m/yr of permanent cost** (author's estimate) — i.e. the annualised regime cost alone approaches a third of the headline $160m settlement every year.

**Barrick (February–April 2025).** Under the agreement Barrick signed, it would pay 275 billion CFA (~$438m) in return for release of detained employees, return of seized gold and restart of Loulo-Gounkoto ([Reuters, 19 Feb 2025](https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/barrick-gold-signs-agreement-with-mali-end-mining-dispute-2025-02-19)). Timeline of coercion: four senior Loulo-Gounkoto employees briefly detained 27 Sept 2024, released 1 Oct, re-arrested and charged 25 Nov 2024 and held awaiting trial; an arrest warrant was reported for CEO Mark Bristow and the complex's GM on 5 Dec 2024; gold shipments blocked 16 Dec; ~3 tonnes (~$245m) seized 11 Jan 2025 and moved to the state-owned Banque Malienne de Solidarité, which Mali planned to liquidate to fund operations; operations suspended 14 Jan 2025 ([CIM Magazine, 17 Apr 2025](https://magazine.cim.org/en/news/2025/mali-closes-barrick-gold-office-amid-ongoing-mining-dispute-en); [Reuters, 26 Nov 2024](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/four-barrick-gold-employees-detained-mali-sources-say-2024-11-26); [TRT Afrika, 15 Jan 2025](https://www.trtafrika.com/english/article/1c6a3e09e3d7)). Barrick had already paid $85m in October 2024 under a framework, and $460m to the Malian state during 2024 ([CIM](https://magazine.cim.org/en/news/2025/mali-closes-barrick-gold-office-amid-ongoing-mining-dispute-en); [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/barrick-gold-signs-agreement-with-mali-end-mining-dispute-2025-02-19)). *Whether the $85m sits inside the $438m is not stated in the admitted sources — an unresolved evidence gap.*

## Mechanism: why the discount persists

1. **Rule change, not bill change.** The August 2023 code raised the state's stake (10% with an option to buy a further 20%), and reporting in February 2025 describes a new law requiring divestment of 35% of new projects to Malian investors and royalties rising from ~6% to 10.5% ([CIM](https://magazine.cim.org/en/news/2025/mali-closes-barrick-gold-office-amid-ongoing-mining-dispute-en); [EY, April 2025](https://www.ey.com/content/dam/ey-unified-site/ey-com/en-au/insights/mining-metals/documents/ey-the-2025-risks-and-opportunities-for-the-gold-mining-sector-240425-002.pdf)). Applying the 6%→10.5% delta to Barrick's Q4 realised price of $2,657/oz is ~$120/oz, or ~$55m/yr attributable at 2024 volumes; a move from 80% to 70% economic ownership would cede ~58koz attributable (author's estimates from [Barrick Q4 2024 presentation](https://s25.q4cdn.com/322814910/files/doc_presentations/2025/02/Barrick_Q4_2024_Results_Presentation.pdf)). Capitalising a plausible combined erosion of ~$150m/yr for 8 years at 8% gives ≈ **$862m** — roughly twice the headline settlement. The settlement is the entry fee; the fiscal architecture is the annuity.
2. **Enforcement risk is not diversifiable.** Detention of executives as a negotiating instrument and seizure of inventory convert a contractual dispute into a *property-rights* discount. Barrick itself booked a **$484m goodwill impairment** on the Loulo-Gounkoto CGU (carrying value $3,564m vs fair value less costs of disposal $3,080m — a 13.6% write-down) and recorded the ICSID filing of 18 Dec 2024 ([Q4 MD&A](https://minedocs.com/28/Barrick-MDA-2024.pdf); [Q4 presentation](https://s25.q4cdn.com/322814910/files/doc_presentations/2025/02/Barrick_Q4_2024_Results_Presentation.pdf)).
3. **The market already priced Mali at or below zero.** Barrick's February 2025 deck states that "market based multiples imply negative value for Barrick's assets outside of NGM and copper," naming Loulo-Gounkoto and Kibali ([Q4 presentation](https://s25.q4cdn.com/322814910/files/doc_presentations/2025/02/Barrick_Q4_2024_Results_Presentation.pdf)). Against FY2024 attributable EBITDA of $5,185m and $45.52bn market capitalisation on 24 April ([Globe and Mail, 24 Apr 2025](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/ABX-T/pressreleases/32031112/barrick-gold-stock-analysis-q1-2025-earnings-and-future-growth-prospects)), EV/EBITDA was ≈8.9x (author's estimate) — while, per January reporting, the stock was down ~12% over the prior year as gold rose ~30% ([Motley Fool Canada, 15 Jan 2025](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/barrick-gold-stock-buy-sell-164500930.html)). Consistently, the $438m news produced only a **+3.37% TSX move** ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/barrick-gold-signs-agreement-with-mali-end-mining-dispute-2025-02-19)): resolution was already assumed.

## Mechanism: Loulo-Gounkoto's operational viability

The orebody case is strong: 578koz produced in 2024 (100% basis) at 4.73 g/t average grade, 91% recovery, $828/oz total cash costs, $1,218/oz cost of sales, EBITDA $598m, capex $307m. Q4 income was already negative (–$13m) solely because export restrictions cut sales to 47koz against 156koz produced ([Q4 presentation](https://s25.q4cdn.com/322814910/files/doc_presentations/2025/02/Barrick_Q4_2024_Results_Presentation.pdf)). Attributable output is ~11.8% of Barrick's 2024 gold production and Mali was ~8.3% of revenue ($1.07bn / $12.92bn) — material, not existential (author's estimates). The viability threat is operational decay, not geology: guidance was cut to 3.2–3.5Moz from 3.9Moz, Loulo-Gounkoto was excluded from 2025 guidance entirely, and the five-year plan assumed restart only "from March 1, 2025." Sustained stoppages degrade reserve sequencing, workforce and contractor capacity, while Mali's own industrial gold output fell 23% y/y in 2024 — evidence the value destruction is bilateral.

## Counterarguments

- **Mali needs the revenue.** Barrick contributed $460m in 2024 and was expected to add ~$550m in 2025; a shuttered mine is a self-harming negotiating tactic ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/barrick-gold-signs-agreement-with-mali-end-mining-dispute-2025-02-19)).
- **Cooperation restores access.** B2Gold settled a tax dispute in September 2024 and kept operating ([CIM](https://magazine.cim.org/en/news/2025/mali-closes-barrick-gold-office-amid-ongoing-mining-dispute-en)).
- **The discount is multi-causal.** Nevada Gold Mines' accounting structure, uncredited copper optionality and sector-wide equity-gold decoupling may explain more of the de-rating than Mali alone.
- **Legal leverage is real.** An ICSID claim plus Mali's need for foreign capital raises the cost of expropriation ([African Law & Business, 13 Jan 2025](https://www.africanlawbusiness.com/news/mali-faces-gold-mining-arbitration)).

## Scenarios (as at the cutoff, not forecasts)

| Scenario | Trigger | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Base (~50%) | Deal executed in H2 2025; $438m paid; employees and gold returned | Modest multiple repair from an already-negative implied Mali value; restart within 1–2 quarters at ~400–500koz (100% basis) |
| Adverse (~30%) | Non-execution, expropriation or state "administration" | Discount persists; possible further impairment of the $3,080m FVLCD; structural loss of output and ownership |
| Favourable (~20%) | Rapid execution plus record gold prices | Re-rating as the "unrealized value" narrative gains traction; ~$450–500m attributable EBITDA recovery in 2026 (author's estimate) |

## Uncertainties and disclosure

Mali's formal approval, the new convention's fiscal terms, whether the $85m overlaps the $438m, and the final state-ownership and royalty formula were unresolved at the cutoff; peer multiples for a formal relative comparison were unavailable in admitted sources. The Finnhub GOLD company-news call returned no records (coverage gap, not proof of absence) and the OpenBB gold-price call failed, so price context rests on Barrick's disclosed realised price and dated reporting.

question: How do PTTEP’s recent strategic actions—including the divestment of North American assets, the acquisition of Jadestone’s Sinphuhorm stake, and intensified drilling campaigns in Sarawak—impact the feasibility of its 900,000 boe/d production target for 2030 amid ongoing recovery challenges at the Erawan gas field?
report:
# PTTEP: Do the 2025 Portfolio Moves Make 900,000 boe/d by 2030 Feasible?

**Research date basis: evidence published on or before 21 July 2025. Facts, inference and scenarios are labelled separately.**

## 1. Direct answer

The three named strategic actions are **directionally consistent with PTTEP's stated gas/LNG-weighted strategy but numerically immaterial to a 900,000 boe/d 2030 outcome**. On the admitted evidence, the Sinphuhorm buy-in adds roughly **1,700–2,000 boe/d**, a quantified set of other disclosed adders (Algeria Touat, Arthit contract uplift, Hassi Bir Rekaiz phase 2) totals only about **45,000–50,000 boe/d**, versus a gap of ~**393,000 boe/d** between the 2025 budget (507,000 boe/d) and 900,000. That is ~**12%** of the gap. Feasibility therefore does not hinge on these deals; it hinges on (a) holding the Erawan–Bongkot plateau against steep mature-field decline, (b) 2026–2027+ ramp-ups (Ghasha/Dalma, Abu Dhabi Waset, Malaysia greenfields, Algeria phase 2, Mozambique restart), and (c) further large acquisitions not disclosed pre-cutoff. **On pre-cutoff evidence, 900,000 boe/d in 2030 looks infeasible without a step-change in capital deployment that PTTEP's own disclosed budgets do not yet support.** Note also that no admitted pre-cutoff document states a "900,000 boe/d by 2030" corporate target (see §7).

## 2. Facts: the documented volume trajectory and capital plan

- 2024 average sales volume **488,794 boe/d**, +6% y/y; 2024 revenue THB 327,415 mn (USD 9,273 mn); net profit THB 78,824 mn (USD 2,227 mn) — [PTTEP, 30 Jan 2025](https://www.pttep.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/1039/pttep-announces-2024-performance-and-2025-operational-plan-investing-over-thb-261-billion-to-continuously-ensure-national-energy-security).
- Q1/2025 average sales volume **484,218 boe/d**, +2% y/y, "primarily driven by higher petroleum production from the G1/61 Project"; realised price USD 45.74/boe — [PTTEP, 25 Apr 2025](https://www.pttep.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/1053/pttep-reports-operating-results-for-the-first-quarter-of-2025).
- Company budget (Stock Exchange of Thailand filing of 20 Dec 2024): **507,000 boe/d in 2025, rising to 541,000 boe/d in 2026**; 2025 capex **USD 5.3 bn** of a **USD 21.2 bn five-year plan**; total 2025 capex+opex **USD 7.82 bn**, five-year **USD 33.6 bn** — [JPT/SPE, 8 Jan 2025](https://jpt.spe.org/pttep-2025-capex-targets-upstream-gas-lng-projects). (A separate pre-cutoff company summary cited 556,000 boe/d for 2026 — [PTT/NBT, 22 Aug 2024](https://www.facebook.com/nbtworld/posts/ptt-public-company-limited-ptt-has-emphasized-its-commitment-to-reducing-greenho/891594056338059) — an unreconciled discrepancy.)
- Investor deck series (sales volume, '000 boe/d): **2023: 462; 2024: 489; 1H2025: 495**; gas mix **72%**; asset value USD 28.6 bn (June 2025) — [PTTEP at a Glance, cached 2025 edition](https://hub.optiwise.io/storage/129/pttep-at-a-glance/2025/pttep-at-a-glance-3q2025.pdf).

**Inference (arithmetic, `math_calc`):** 507 → 900 requires **12.2%/yr for five years**; from the 2026 plan, **13.6%/yr for four years**. Actual growth 2023 → 2026 plan (462 → 541) was **5.4%/yr** — i.e. the target needs **more than double** the growth rate PTTEP has been delivering and budgeting.

## 3. The three actions, quantified

**Sinphuhorm (Thailand, onshore).** Facts: PTTEP's participating interest rose **80.487% → 90%** effective 16 April 2025, buying Jadestone's 9.52% via APICO LLC for **USD 39.4 mn** cash (USD 35 mn base, effective 1 Jan 2025) plus **USD 3.5 mn** contingent on licence extensions (licences expire 2029 and 2031) — [Jadestone, 16 Apr 2025](https://www.jadestone-energy.com/portfolio-focus-and-optimization-sale-of-sinphuhorm-interest); field produced **105 MMSCFD gas + 222 bbl/d condensate** in 2024 — [PTTEP, 25 Apr 2025](https://www.pttep.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/1053/pttep-reports-operating-results-for-the-first-quarter-of-2025). Inference: 9.52% × (105,000/6 + 222) ≈ **1,687 boe/d**; at the December-2024 gross rate of 122 MMscfd ([OGJ, 24 Mar 2025](https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/article/55276865/horizon-matahio-energy-to-acquire-assets-onshore-thailand-from-exxonmobil)) ≈ **~2,000 boe/d**, i.e. **0.2%** of the 2030 gap and **0.4%** of the 2025 budget. Strategically it consolidates operatorship and adds low-cost, low-decline dry gas (82% modelled recovery factor per OGJ), but it is a reserve/cost-per-unit and energy-security action, not a growth action. The 2029/2031 licence expiries also mean much of the added barrel could roll off at or just before the target year.

**North American divestment.** Gap: **no admitted pre-cutoff source documents a completed or announced "North American" divestment by PTTEP.** The closest admitted evidence is PTTEP's own disclosure that **Australia and Mexico positions are "under relinquishment approval"** in the same investor deck, the long-standing strategy of "rationaliz[ing] our investment portfolio in non-core areas" (e.g. Montara divestment, renegotiated Mariana oil-sands obligations — [PTTEP 2018 Annual Report](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/Z6QXO5CYQFLRE9D9/550357_2018PTTEP%20Annual%20Report.pdf)), and the 2025 pivot of capital toward UAE/Algeria/Malaysia/Mozambique — [JPT/SPE, 8 Jan 2025](https://jpt.spe.org/pttep-2025-capex-targets-upstream-gas-lng-projects). Inference: a North American exit is **volume-dilutive in the near term** (it removes oil-weighted barrels) while being margin-, capital-efficiency- and carbon-intensity-accretive. It therefore makes a *boe-count* target harder and a *value/gas-mix* objective easier — a real tension in the question's framing.

**Sarawak / Malaysia drilling.** Facts: PTTEP's 2025 workplan "accelerate[s] development projects in Malaysia Greenfields ... while fast-tracking exploration projects in both Thailand and Malaysia" ([PTTEP, 30 Jan 2025](https://www.pttep.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/1039/pttep-announces-2024-performance-and-2025-operational-plan-investing-over-thb-261-billion-to-continuously-ensure-national-energy-security)); the plan names production start-up at Malaysian greenfield projects **SK405B, SK417, SK438** ([JPT/SPE, 8 Jan 2025](https://jpt.spe.org/pttep-2025-capex-targets-upstream-gas-lng-projects)); **SK410B (Lang Lebah)** was under **re-engineering within 2025** "for cost reduction and optimal balance between production capacity and investment" ([PTTEP at a Glance](https://hub.optiwise.io/storage/129/pttep-at-a-glance/2025/pttep-at-a-glance-3q2025.pdf)). The regional activity backdrop is PETRONAS targeting **2 MMboe/d by 2027** with ~15 exploration wells/year ([industry summary, 30 Jan 2025](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aznial-rahmat-a3145636_petronas-activity-outlook-for-2025-2027-petronass-activity-7290897104997072896-7m8W) — secondary source). Gap: **no admitted source quantifies Sarawak well counts, volumes or first-gas dates for PTTEP.** Inference: deepwater gas projects sanctioned/re-designed in 2025 typically deliver first gas in **2028–2031**, so Sarawak drilling is largely **post-2030 optionality** and a *reserve replacement* (R/P > 5 years is a stated long-term target — [PTTEP sustainability framework](https://sustainability.pttep.com/en/our-sustainability/sustainability-framework-and-long-term-target)) rather than a 2030 volume lever.

## 4. Erawan: the swing factor

Facts: G1/61 (Erawan, Platong, Satun, Funan) rose **210 → 400 MMSCFD by end-Q2 2023** ([OGJ, 31 Jul 2023](https://www.ogj.com/ogj-survey-downloads/worldwide-production/article/14297140/pttep-increases-natural-gas-production-from-g1-g6-gulf-of-thailand-project)) and **400 → 800 MMSCFD since 20 March 2024**, sustained through 2024–2025 ([PTTEP, 30 Jan 2025](https://www.pttep.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/1039/pttep-announces-2024-performance-and-2025-operational-plan-investing-over-thb-261-billion-to-continuously-ensure-national-energy-security); [Nation Thailand, 20 Mar 2024](https://www.nationthailand.com/business/corporate/40036567)). PTTEP holds a **60% operated interest** (Mubadala 40%); the Erawan/Bongkot pair supplies ~**60% of domestic gas consumption**, with an explicit commitment to hold ~**1,500 MMcf/d** combined ([JPT/SPE, 8 Jan 2025](https://jpt.spe.org/pttep-2025-capex-targets-upstream-gas-lng-projects)); capital to reverse the decline only began in **2022** after Chevron-transfer delays, and in 2023 the plan was "maintain gas sales at 400 MMSCFD ... continue drilling new production wells" plus four wellhead platforms ([PTTEP opportunity-day deck, 2 Nov 2023](http://www.chemwinfo.com/private_folder/2023/23_Nov/Pttep_RS_oppday-20231102-0119213777.pdf)).

Inference: 800 MMSCFD ≈ **133,000 boe/d** of gas-equivalent, i.e. ~**26%** of the 2025 budget in one project. The "recovery challenge" is therefore a **plateau problem, not a ramp problem**: at an assumed 10% natural decline from that plateau (analyst assumption, not from sources), PTTEP would surrender ~13,000 boe/d per year unless infill drilling and new platforms keep pace — the same volume the entire Sinphuhorm deal added, every five weeks. More broadly, offsetting a ~5% base decline on the 72% gas-weighted book costs roughly **18,000 boe/d per year** (~90,000 boe/d over five years) before any growth is achieved.

## 5. Scenario bridges to 2030 (illustrative, built on admitted 2025–26 anchors)

| Scenario | 2030 outcome | Assumptions |
|---|---|---|
| **Stall** | ~**609,000 boe/d** | +3%/yr after 2026; Erawan decays from 800 MMSCFD; Mozambique late; greenfields slip |
| **Base execution** | ~**679,000 boe/d** | 6%/yr off 507: Erawan plateau held, Touat ~16,000 boe/d ([OGJ/PTTEP](https://jpt.spe.org/pttep-2025-capex-targets-upstream-gas-lng-projects)), Ghasha/Dalma first gas early 2026, HBR phase-2 ramp to 30 KBPD (2029) — [PTTEP MD&A, 31 Jan 2024](https://market.sec.or.th/public/idisc/Download?FILEID=dat%2Fnews%2F202401%2F0355NWS300120241805050120E.pdf) |
| **Bull** | ~**817,000 boe/d** | 10%/yr: Waset first gas 2027, SK405B/SK417/SK438 startups, MTJDA expansion, strong pricing |
| **Target-consistent** | **900,000 boe/d** | Requires **12.2%/yr** and ~**393,000 boe/d** of net additions — only ~12% of which is quantified in disclosed projects |

Mechanism summary: divestment proceeds and relinquished non-core capital are **redeployed** into gas/LNG where PTTEP earns 70–75% EBITDA margins and long-term GSAs ([PTTEP at a Glance](https://hub.optiwise.io/storage/129/pttep-at-a-glance/2025/pttep-at-a-glance-3q2025.pdf)); acquisitions of partners' stakes (Bongkot 100% after TotalEnergies' 33.33% transfer, Sinphuhorm 90%) **raise net share of existing barrels without exploration risk**; drilling in Sarawak/Thailand **replenishes reserves** with a 3–5 year lag. Counterargument: each lever either shrinks the barrel count (exits), adds trivially (Sinphuhorm), or matures after 2030 (deepwater), while USD 5.3 bn/yr capex is already committed to a 507→541 trajectory — leaving no disclosed funding envelope for a doubling.

## 6. Uncertainties

Volume conversion (boe) uses 6 Mcf = 1 boe; PTTEP's own deck states gas is ~72% of sales; budget vs. 1H25 actual (507 vs 495) shows the company running ~2% below plan; realised price falling to USD 45.74/boe (Q1/25) pressures the self-funding of capex out of 2024's USD 2.2 bn net profit; Mozambique remained under force majeure pending restart guarantees ([JPT/SPE](https://jpt.spe.org/pttep-2025-capex-targets-upstream-gas-lng-projects)).

## 7. Verification limits and gaps

1. **The 900,000 boe/d 2030 target itself is unverified** in admitted pre-cutoff sources; disclosed official guidance stops at 2026 (541,000 boe/d), and stated long-term targets are qualitative (growth, R/P > 5 years, net zero 2050).
2. **No admitted source confirms a North American divestment** — analysis is framed as a portfolio logic, not an established event.
3. **No admitted source quantifies PTTEP's Sarawak drilling programme**; one targeted search returned no results (coverage gap, not evidence of absence).
4. **Skill-based market data unavailable:** the Finnhub news call for PTTEP.BK failed (CLI exit 1); OpenBB was not used as index/FX/yield data are not material here. Consequently no market-price or analyst-expectation evidence is included, and no valuation model was run.
5. The PTTEP "at a Glance" PDF cached under a June-2025 stamp carries "last update: July 2025" markings; only items clearly dated on/before 21 July 2025 were used, and post-cutoff lines (e.g. 25/31 July 2025) were excluded.

report:
# Stats Canada's +10.9% soybean stocks vs. China's 12 MMT commitment: North American export competition and global price stability through Q1 2026

*Point-in-time research note. Evidence cutoff 2025-11-04 UTC. Facts, inference and forward scenarios are labelled separately.*

## Direct answer (inference from admitted evidence)

The two data points are not actually in conflict, and reading them as a conflict overstates the disinflationary punch that Chinese buying could deliver. The +10.9% inventory readings are **backward-looking evidence of a demand failure** (China bought almost no U.S. or marginal Canadian beans during mid-2025), while the 12 MMT commitment is **unverified, forward, calendar-year-2025 U.S.-specific** purchase language announced on 2025-10-30. Through Q1 2026 the most likely outcome is: (1) a **front-loaded, U.S.-skewed export window** in Nov 2025–Jan 2026 that squeezes Canadian and South American bean competition in the same ports; (2) a **narrower, not reversed, inventory overhang**, because commitments of 12 MMT plus 25 MMT/year sit at or below historical norms; and (3) **price stability only through roughly February 2026**, after which Brazil's record crop re-asserts a supply ceiling. Quantitatively, 12 MMT ≈ **441 million bushels** (12 × 36.74 bu/t) — meaningful, but not enough to absorb a North American supply glut of the scale documented below.

## Premise check: which "10.9%"? (fact)

Two separate Statistics Canada releases — both pre-cutoff — reported a **10.9% year-over-year soybean inventory increase**: stocks of **4.2 Mt at December 31, 2024** (on-farm +34.3% to 2.8 Mt, commercial −18.0% to 1.4 Mt), released 2025-02-07 ([statcan.gc.ca](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250207/dq250207c-eng.htm)), and **2.4 Mt at March 31, 2025** (on-farm +11.1%, commercial +10.6% to 988 kt), released 2025-05-08 ([statcan.gc.ca](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250508/dq250508a-eng.htm)). Both describe the **2024-25 crop year** (Canada's soybean crop year runs Sept 1–Aug 31). No Stats Canada inventory reading published on or before the cutoff quantified 2025-26 stocks; the November 2025 Field Crop Survey results were scheduled for **2025-12-04**, after the cutoff ([statcan.gc.ca, 2025-08-28](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250828/dq250828c-eng.htm)). A Sept 2025 Stats Canada inventories report showed total crop-year-end (31 July 2025) inventories **22% lower year-over-year**, driven by canola, wheat, oats and flax drawdowns; the soybean line is not quantified in the admitted excerpt ([Sask Wheat, 2025-09-15](https://saskwheat.ca/wheat-market-outlook/wheat-market-outlook-september-15-2025)). **Analytical consequence:** the +10.9% figure should be treated as a *carried-in* inventory signal, not a current 2025-26 surplus reading.

## Evidence base

**Canadian supply/demand (AAFC outlook, 2025-09-26).** 2024-25 exports were **5.4 Mt (+10%, second-highest on record)** with carry-out stocks a five-year high at **0.56 Mt**; China was the largest buyer of Canadian soybeans at **1.04 Mt**, ahead of Iran (0.77 Mt) and Algeria (0.55 Mt); the track-Chatham average price fell to **$487/t** from $572/t ([producer.com PDF](https://static.producer.com/wp-content/uploads/2025-09-29154258/Canada-Outlook-for-Principal-Field-Crops_202509.pdf)). For 2025-26 AAFC forecast production **7.1 Mt (−6% y/y, fourth-largest on record)**, total supply 8.1 Mt, domestic use 2.2 Mt (−9%), exports 5.4 Mt and carry-out 0.55 Mt.

**The commitment (2025-10-30, Busan).** Per the White House fact sheet as reported: China will buy **at least 12 MMT of U.S. soybeans in the last two months of 2025** and **at least 25 MMT in each of 2026, 2027 and 2028**, plus resumed sorghum/hardwood logs and reduced Chinese tariffs on U.S. farm goods ([AgWeb, 2025-11-04](https://www.agweb.com/news/policy/politics/setting-record-straight-what-china-actually-agreed-buy-and-when-those-ag-pur)). Context: China bought **~23 MMT (841 MMBU)** of U.S. beans in 2024-25 and averaged **29 MMT in 2020-24** ([Iowa Soybean Association timeline, updated 2025-11-03](https://www.iasoybeans.com/newsroom/article/tracking-us-and-china-soybean-trade)). American Farm Bureau (2025-11-03) notes Nov–Dec U.S. exports to China averaged **9.5 MMT** over the last decade, so 12 MMT would be the fourth-highest two-month volume ever, taking calendar-2025 purchases to ~**18 MMT** against a ~**27 MMT** historical annual average — i.e. **33% below trend** ([fb.org](https://www.fb.org/intel/markets/china-phase-two-what-we-know-right-now)).

**Pre-announcement demand hole (facts).** U.S. shipments to China: 985 MMBU in 2024 = 51% of total U.S. soybean exports; only **218 MMBU Jan–Aug 2025** (29% of exports), with June–August effectively zero ([farmdoc daily, 2025-09-22](https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/2025/09/us-soybean-harvest-starts-with-no-sign-of-chinese-buying-as-brazil-sets-export-record.html)). USDA projected U.S. ag exports to China of $17bn in 2025 (−30% y/y) and **$9bn in 2026**, the lowest since the 2018 trade war ([fb.org, 2025-10-02](https://www.fb.org/intel/markets/agricultural-trade-china-steps-back-from-u-s-soybeans)). Company-level confirmation of the glut: ADM cut FY2025 adjusted EPS guidance from **$4.00 to $3.25–3.50** (vs $3.84 expected) on 2025-11-04, citing biofuel and trade uncertainty, "awaiting clarity" on the China deal, with press coverage stating "bumper crops in North and South America are filling grain elevators" and China's limited purchases "created a supply glut" ([Finnhub/ADM news](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=80a2170936c76c79a4c9f342e453f9414d2278d75e6f2256c00538c2a4f22a6a), [2](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=b352e9bd3164c8f828e3b64899e851ba485c9c973685bbbef16a2e2bc10d7fce), [3](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=36d51c8c4d9d449b9f1381b9f3c90a2d39f15e9eee3b13cfa0e8c8bd424ac6b4)).

**Price and basis evidence.** CBOT November soybeans traded around **$10.30¾/bu** (peak $10.38, highest since Sept 19) on 2025-10-22 ([ukragroconsult](https://ukragroconsult.com/en/news/us-soybean-prices-rise-amid-expectations-of-renewed-chinese-purchases)); ISA reports the bushel price rose **more than 60¢ on the Oct 30 news**, Northern Plains and port **basis ticked up**, and **U.S. port prices moved close to Brazilian levels** — while, as of Nov 1, **China had signed no contract** ([iasoybeans.com](https://www.iasoybeans.com/newsroom/article/tracking-us-and-china-soybean-trade)). Scott Irwin (2025-10-20) estimated that adjusting for non-Chinese destinations, total 2025-26 exports were closer to **1.43–1.47 bn bu vs USDA's 1.685 bn bu**, implying roughly **+250 MMBU** to ending stocks and ~**500 MMBU (12.5% stocks-to-use)** ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/scotthirwin_soybeans-china-trade-activity-7386034964032790528-f2Np)). FX: USDCAD moved from ~1.3738 (2025-09-01) to ~1.4055 (2025-11-04), a **+2.3% Canadian-dollar depreciation** (OpenBB/yfinance daily observation — retrospective vintage, not a frozen publication), which improves CAD-denominated farmer economics and modestly sharpens Canadian USD offer prices.

## Mechanisms and scenarios for Q1 2026 (inference)

1. **Demand redirection, not demand creation.** Chinese buying concentrates in the Pacific Northwest and Gulf in Nov–Jan. Because U.S. port prices are now near Brazilian parity, Canadian beans (net-backs out of Chatham/Thunder Bay, and Pacific routing) lose marginal price competitiveness precisely in China's historical Nov–Mar purchase window. **Inference:** Canadian 2025-26 exports of 5.4 Mt become harder in Q1, with carry-out stocks drifting toward/above the 0.55 Mt forecast, echoing the +10.9% build pattern of early 2025.
2. **Offsetting Canadian lever.** A weaker CAD plus non-China demand (Iran, Algeria, Bangladesh/Vietnam-type crush buyers) partially cushions volume; AAFC's Chatham price forecast was already "up slightly" for 2025-26.
3. **Window closing.** Brazil's Conab projected a record **177.6 Mt** for 2025-26 (USDA 175 Mt; private 176.5–181 Mt) with record **~112 Mt exports**, roughly matching China's total forecast imports ([Michigan Farm News, 2025-10-16](https://www.michiganfarmnews.com/brazil-projects-record-soybean-crop-and-growing-exports-citing-demand-from-china); [Terrain, 2025-10-06](https://www.terrainag.com/insights/can-the-u-s-crush-the-competition)). Chinese buyers also booked Brazilian cargoes for December and March–July 2026, and Argentine soy after Buenos Aires suspended its 26% export tax following the U.S. support package — which ISA said let China "bypass U.S. soybean farmers through February 2026." **Inference:** from Feb–Mar 2026 the marginal buyer switches back to South America, capping any Q1 rally.
4. **Scenarios (probabilities are judgemental, not modelled).** *Base (~55%):* partial delivery, 17–20 MMT CY2025 Chinese purchases, CBOT ranges $9.80–$11.00/bu, basis firm in the U.S. and soft in Canada; moderate price stability. *Bull-for-North America (~25%):* full 12 MMT delivered plus early 25 MMT 2026 signing; U.S. exports near 1.6 bn bu, stocks nearer 400 MMBU, prices bid above $11 but with freight/river-logistics bottlenecks and a sharper post-Brazil-correction decline in Q2. *Bear (~20%):* headlines without contracts (as at Nov 1); futures unwind toward Sept lows, and the inventory overhang persists — the pattern ADM's guidance cut already priced.

## Counterarguments and residual risks

Beijing had not publicly confirmed the commitment at cutoff, and Phase One precedent shows gradual diversion to other suppliers. Record U.S. domestic crush competes for the same bushels (biofuel-policy clarity not expected before spring 2026), muting exportable surplus. The U.S. government shutdown delayed official statistics (noted 2025-11-04), degrading shipment verification. China's import demand may be nearer 100 MMT than USDA's 112 MMT, capping every exporter.

## Evidence gaps

Stats Canada's 2025-26 production/stocks detail (2025-12-04 release) and November 2025 U.S. export-sales/inspection data fall outside the cutoff; exact Nov 3–4 January-2026 CBOT settlements and Chinese contract confirmations were unavailable in admitted sources; no frozen-vintage WASDE/FRED soybean price series was accessible, so prices come from dated news documents.

question: Given Tyvaso's 58.8% contribution to United Therapeutics' revenue and the series of failed injunctions against Liquidia's Yutrepia in mid-2025, how will the potential label expansion of Tyvaso into Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) mitigate competitive risks and protect UTHR’s valuation through 2026?
report:
# Tyvaso Concentration, the Failed Liquidia Injunctions, and Whether an IPF Label Can Protect UTHR Through 2026

**Information cutoff: 2025-08-05. Facts below are limited to documents published on or before that date. Inference and forward scenarios are explicitly labelled.**

## Direct answer

An IPF label expansion is a *real but slow-acting* hedge against a *fast-acting* competitive threat. As of the cutoff, United Therapeutics' (UTHR) exposure was exactly as the premise states — total Tyvaso revenue of **$469.6m on total revenue of $798.6m in Q2 2025 = 58.8%** of sales ([Q2 2025 release](https://ir.unither.com/press-releases/2025/07-30-2025-113026622)) — and Liquidia's Yutrepia was already shipping to patients with **no injunction outstanding**, because UTHR's emergency-relief motions had been denied ([Liquidia, 2 Jun 2025](https://liquidia.com/news-releases/news-release-details/liquidia-schedules-first-commercial-shipment-yutrepiatm)). But the IPF pathway (the **TETON** programme) could not contribute revenue inside the 2026 window: TETON 2 data were guided to **September 2025**, TETON 1 data to **first half 2026**, with filing and review still ahead ([Q2 2025 release](https://ir.unither.com/press-releases/2025/07-30-2025-113026622); [TETON 1 enrolment, 4 Feb 2025](https://ir.unither.com/press-releases/2025/02-04-2025-120131472)). So through 2026 the IPF option protects valuation mainly **through the cost of equity narrative — pipeline optionality that offsets a temporarily eroding cash-flow base — not through revenue.** Its revenue power only becomes credible for 2027+.

Two mechanisms do most of the medium-term protection: (i) IPF addresses a US population of **">100,000 patients"** with **only two approved drugs, which "only slow the course of disease progression"** ([TETON 1 release](https://ir.unither.com/press-releases/2025/02-04-2025-120131472)) — an order of magnitude larger than the ~8,800-patient Tyvaso base estimated by a third party ([Bleecker Street, 29 Jul 2025](https://www.bleeckerstreetresearch.com/research/uthr-lqda)); and (ii) the same molecule, device and field force are reused, so incremental patients are almost pure margin.

## Verified facts

**Concentration is high and rising.** Tyvaso was 45.1% of revenue in 2022 ($873m) ([Bloomberg Law, 20 Dec 2023](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/liquidias-yutrepia-path-clear-as-utc-loses-axed-patent-appeal)), 56.3% in 2024 ($1,620.4m of ~$2.88bn, +31% y/y) ([4Q24 release, 26 Feb 2025](https://ir.unither.com/~/media/Files/U/United-Therapeutics-IR/documents/press-releases/2024/2025-02-26-4q24-earnings-release.pdf)) and 58.8% in Q2 2025. The franchise still grew 18% y/y (DPI +22%, nebulized +10%) even after Yutrepia launched; Remodulin fell 9%.

**Litigation state.** Yutrepia was approved **23 May 2025** for PAH *and* PH-ILD on the same day Tyvaso DPI's new-clinical-investigation exclusivity expired ([Liquidia 10-K, 19 Mar 2025](https://www.liquidia.com/static-files/3e01efd2-5158-4131-830d-63108709df42); [Hunterbrook, 23 May 2025](https://hntrbrk.com/breaking-news/liquidia-united)); first commercial shipment followed **2 June 2025**. On **30 May 2025** the M.D.N.C. denied UTHR's TRO/preliminary injunction on the '782 patent, finding UTHR "not likely to succeed on the merits," that lost sales were "speculative," and that the public interest favoured denial ([Robins Kaplan Q2 2025 bulletin](https://www.robinskaplan.com/newsroom/insights/generically-speaking-hatch-waxman-bulletin-2025-q2-united-therapeutics-corp-v-liquidia-techs-inc)). That followed a denied PI in Delaware on the '327 patent (31 May 2024), the Federal Circuit's invalidation of '793, and an October 2024 Supreme Court refusal — hence "a series." **Important qualification: the merits cases are not over.** UTHR still asserts patents expiring as late as January 2042, and Liquidia's own filings warn an adverse ruling could still restrict Yutrepia to PAH or force royalties/damages ([Liquidia 10-K](https://www.liquidia.com/static-files/3e01efd2-5158-4131-830d-63108709df42)).

**Balance-sheet shock absorbers (facts).** At 30 June 2025: cash, equivalents and marketable investments **$4,966.4m**, total liabilities **$734.4m**, equity **$7,173.6m**, diluted EPS $6.41, operating margin 45.6% ($364.5m/$798.6m), plus a **$1bn buyback** authorised to 31 Mar 2026 — explicitly framed by the board as confidence in "upcoming catalysts" and "our share price potential" ([Q2 2025 release](https://ir.unither.com/press-releases/2025/07-30-2025-113026622)).

## Quantified bridge (scenario arithmetic, clearly labelled assumptions)

Using admitted inputs only: FY2024 Tyvaso $1,620.4m; the third-party estimate of ~8,800 Tyvaso patients ⇒ **~$184k revenue per patient-year**; Q2 2025 operating margin 45.6%; 48.3m diluted shares; 10-year U.S. Treasury of 4.22% at 5 Aug 2025 ([Fed H.15 via OpenBB](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/)) used as a *discount floor*, so present values are upper bounds.

| Item | Base case (−11%) | Bear case (−28%) |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 Tyvaso revenue loss vs 2024 | **$178.2m** | **$453.7m** |
| Operating income at 45.6% | $81.4m | $207.1m |
| Diluted EPS impact | **$1.68** | **$4.29** |
| "Tyvaso-equivalent" IPF patients needed to offset | **968** (0.97% of >100k) | **2,464** (2.46% of >100k) |

*Reading:* the erosion scenarios published before the cutoff (Bleecker Street's −11%/−28% Tyvaso and −22%/−37% EPS 2024→2026; management's own view was only 5% share loss) are dwarfed arithmetically by IPF: **fewer than 1,000 IPF patients — about 1% of the stated US pool — neutralise the entire base case**, and ~2.5% neutralise the bear case. A 3,000-patient IPF franchise ≈ $552m revenue, ≈ $252m operating income, ≈ **+$5.22 diluted EPS**, with a five-year PV of ≈$1.1bn at the 4.22% floor. *These are mechanical illustrations, not forecasts:* they assume IPF patients generate the same revenue/patient as the current Tyvaso base and ignore launch, pricing, payer and tolerability frictions.

## Mechanisms, counterarguments, scenarios

**Why the IPF label mitigates.** (1) Diversification: a new indication changes the 58.8% single-product dependency into one product across three indications, so Yutrepia — a *DPI* — competes only with Tyvaso DPI, while a nebulized IPF label opens a channel Liquidia cannot copy without its own IPF trials. (2) Duration: the IPF label is supported by UTHR's own patents/programme rather than the Orange Book patents already lost or doubted, and PPF plus an EMA filing (partner Ferrer) extend the runway. (3) Multiple: for a company with $4.97bn liquidity, an approved IPF drug shifts the terminal-growth assumption for the largest revenue line, which matters far more in a valuation than one quarter's Tyvaso growth.

**Counterarguments.** (a) *Timing mismatch*: with TETON 2 in Sept 2025 and TETON 1 in 1H 2026, plus bridging studies for DPI, no material IPF revenue is plausible in 2026 — mitigation is sentiment, not cash flow. (b) *Binary risk*: FVC-based IPF endpoints can miss; INCREASE post-hoc gains (+2.5% at week 8, +3.5% at week 16) were subgroup signals, not registration evidence. (c) *Substitution, not addition*: physicians in the July survey flagged Yutrepia's tolerability and dosing flexibility; the same argument cuts against treprostinil in IPF, where cough/bronchospasm warnings are prominent. (d) *Litigation overhang cuts both ways*: if UTHR later wins on the merits, damages/injunctions help cash flow but signal enforcement risk; if it loses, DPI erosion persists beyond 2026. (e) *IPF incumbents* (two approved antifibrotics) anchor payer willingness-to-pay.

**Scenarios for 2026.** Bull: TETON 2 and TETON 1 positive, sNDA accepted, DPI bridging path clear → concentration falls below ~50% on a forward basis and the 5%–30% share-loss debate becomes immaterial. Base: TETON 2 positive, TETON 1 mixed/late → modest 2026 Tyvaso share loss (~$178m) offset by Orenitram/Unituxin growth and the buyback; IPF revenue lands 2027. Bear: TETON misses plus Yutrepia accelerates toward the 28% case (~$454m, ~$4.29 EPS) with no near-term IPF offset.

**Monitoring (post-cutoff, unverified here).** TETON 2 topline; TETON 1; '782/'327 merits and appeal rulings; Yutrepia script/RAR tracking; Tyvaso DPI gross-to-net; buyback execution.

## Evidence gaps
Finnhub returned **no** UTHR company news for 1 Jun–5 Aug 2025 (coverage gap, not absence of news). No admissible pre-cutoff share price/market-cap source was obtained, so EV, P/E and P/S multiples are **not** computed here. "EROPA" could not be verified in pre-cutoff sources as the IPF vehicle; the documented IPF route is the TETON programme with a separate DPI label-expansion intent. OpenBB treasury data are retrospective observations, not frozen vintages. Patient counts, revenue-per-patient and share-capture percentages rest partly on one non-peer-reviewed third-party survey and on management's own statements — treat as scenario inputs.

# Joseph Feldman's Mid-2025 Retail Split: Target/Best Buy vs. Walmart/Costco

**Research cutoff: 2025-07-21. All evidence below was published on or before that date.**

## First, a correction to the premise

Joseph (Joe) Feldman is **not** a Wells Fargo analyst. Every pre-cutoff source located identifies him as the retail analyst at **Telsey Advisory Group** ([MarketBeat analyst profile](https://www.marketbeat.com/all-access/analyst-rankings/738); [U.S. News, 2025-05-21](https://money.usnews.com/investing/articles/best-equities-to-buy-in-todays-stock-market); [The Globe and Mail, 2025-05-03](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/COST/pressreleases/32200028/telsey-advisory-keeps-their-buy-rating-on-costco-cost)). Wells Fargo's big-box retail analyst, **Edward Kelly**, separately cut Target to Equal-weight with a $142 target (from $170) in the same week ([Bloomberg via Facebook, 2025-05-22](https://www.facebook.com/bloombergbusiness/posts/discount-retailer-ross-shares-fell-after-pulling-its-full-year-profit-outlook-du/1116057463713679); [Business Insider via Facebook, 2025-06-16](https://www.facebook.com/insider/posts/we-visited-three-target-stores-across-the-us-to-get-a-sense-of-what-the-retail-c/1085425446778391)). The two analysts' actions converged, so the substance of the question still holds — but it is analyzed here as **Feldman/Telsey**.

A second premise refinement: in mid-2025 Feldman **downgraded Target** but **did not downgrade Best Buy**. He cut Best Buy's price target to $90 (from $95) while *maintaining* Outperform ([MarketBeat ratings history](https://www.marketbeat.com/all-access/analyst-rankings/738); for the prior $95 Outperform stance see [Sahm Capital, 2024-03-20](https://www.sahmcapital.com/news/content/telsey-advisory-group-upgrades-best-buy-co-to-outperform-raises-price-target-to-95-2024-03-20)). What he did to both was **cut estimates and targets**; only Target lost its rating.

## Direct answer

Feldman's May–June 2025 actions encode a **trade-down bifurcation**: money flowing *into* value, consumables and membership-fee formats (Walmart, Costco) and *out of* discretionary, big-ticket and non-price-driven formats (Target, Best Buy, Deckers), with tariffs converting that mix shift into an earnings-risk event for the second group. The divergence is visible in **direction of revisions**, not in headline valuations: his cut names actually screen *cheaper* on upside-to-target than his favourites.

## The numbers behind the split

Management cut FY EPS guidance to **$7–$9 from $8.80–$9.80**, a **14.0% midpoint reduction**, citing tariffs and weak consumer sentiment ([Star Tribune](https://www.startribune.com/target-c-suite-executive-shakeup-sales-decline-michael-fiddelke-christina-hennington/601343297)).

**Best Buy (Q1 FY2026, reported 2025-05-29).** Revenue $8.767bn, comps **-0.7%**, GAAP EPS $0.95, adjusted $1.15; FY26 adjusted EPS guided to **$6.15–$6.30 from $6.20–$6.60** (-2.7% midpoint), comps to **-1%/+1% from flat/+2%**, revenue to $41.1–41.9bn from $41.4–42.2bn ([Best Buy IR](https://investors.bestbuy.com/News--Events/news/news-details/2025/Best-Buy-Reports-First-Quarter-Results/default.aspx); [Zacks/Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/best-buy-beats-q1-earnings-164400565.html)). Category detail is the bifurcation in microcosm: appliances **-8.1%**, consumer electronics **-5.2%**, entertainment **-13.3%** ([Best Buy IR](https://investors.bestbuy.com/News--Events/news/news-details/2025/Best-Buy-Reports-First-Quarter-Results/default.aspx); [Retail Dive](https://www.retaildive.com/news/best-buy-lowers-guidance-q1-revenue-drops-tariffs/749298)). Management explicitly anchored guidance to **tariffs staying at current levels** and to no material change in consumer behaviour ([earnings call transcript, Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-best-buy-beats-q1-2025-forecasts-shares-dip-93CH-4070500)).

**Walmart (Q1 FY2026, reported 2025-05-15).** Sales +4% cc to $165.6bn; **Walmart US comps +4.5%**, e-commerce +21%; adjusted EPS $0.61 vs $0.58 consensus; **FY guidance maintained** at +3–4% sales and $2.50–$2.60 adjusted EPS ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025-05-15/walmart-wmt-q1-2026-earnings.html); [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/walmart-warns-higher-prices-withholds-second-quarter-profit-guidance-2025-05-15); [call transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-walmarts-q1-2026-earnings-beat-expectations-93CH-4048200)). Even inside Walmart, the split repeats: grocery comped mid-single digits with share gains and health/wellness +high-teens, while **general merchandise declined**, weak in electronics, home and sporting goods.

**Costco.** Q2 (ended 16 Feb) revenue $63.72bn vs $58.44bn, net profit $1.79bn vs $1.74bn; Feldman raised his target from $1,000 (April) to **$1,100 (May)** and reiterated it through early June ([Globe and Mail](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/COST/pressreleases/32200028/telsey-advisory-keeps-their-buy-rating-on-costco-cost); [Sahm Capital](https://www.sahmcapital.com/news/content/value-shoppers-still-show-up-but-costcos-growth-hits-speed-bump-2025-04-04)).

The **Walmart-US vs Target comp spread was 8.3 percentage points** (+4.5% vs -3.8%) in the same macro quarter — the single cleanest quantitative expression of the bifurcation. Sector flows corroborate: Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF +5% YTD vs Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR -7% YTD as of March 2025 ([Invezz/TradingView, 2025-03-09](https://www.tradingview.com/news/invezz:6626fbacb094b:0-consumer-staples-outperform-in-2025-but-here-s-why-investors-may-want-to-reconsider-their-bets-now)).

## Mechanisms

1. **Tariff pass-through hits import-heavy discretionary baskets first.** Both cut firms embedded tariffs in guidance; Walmart's CFO called tariffs "still too high" but kept FY guidance, leaning on scale, 5,000+ price rollbacks and private-brand penetration (+60bps).
2. **Trade-down is zero-sum on traffic.** Value, consumables and membership formats gained share; Target's non-consumables did not. Best Buy's services comped +0.9% while appliances (-8.1%) and electronics (-5.2%) fell — big-ticket is cut first.
3. **Execution visibility.** Feldman cited inconsistent execution; Target's CEO described running "week by week, almost day by day," amid an executive shake-up and boycott-driven traffic loss.
4. **Membership income de-risks forecasting** for Costco/Walmart in a way absent at Target/Best Buy.

## Counterarguments

- **Upside-to-target contradicts a "bearish discretionary" label.** Implied 12-month upside at report-date prices: Best Buy **+27.2%** ($90/$70.73), Target **+18.3%** ($110/$93.01), Walmart **+18.0%** ($115/$97.46), Costco **+9.6%** ($1,100/$1,003.91). His least-favoured name screened cheapest — the divergence is in confidence in the estimate path, not price attractiveness.
- **Not a clean staples-vs-discretionary split.** He kept Outperform on discretionary housing names (Home Depot $455, Lowe's $305) yet held Dollar General/Dollar Tree at Market Perform despite raising targets. Tariff exposure, ticket size and execution explain his actions better than sector labels.
- **Target's gap is partly self-inflicted** (DEI pullback, boycotts), so part of the Walmart–Target spread is idiosyncratic, not consumer bifurcation.
- **Single-analyst, aggregator-recorded evidence**; ratings are ordinal and non-standardised.

## Scenarios (forward-looking, not forecasts)

- **Tariff status quo** (Best Buy's own base case): modest estimate cuts persist; value/membership names compound share.
- **Escalation/pass-through:** discretionary demand destruction deepens; further target cuts even at low multiples; Walmart's withheld Q2 EPS guidance becomes the template.
- **Rate relief:** the 2025-07-18 curve (2Y 3.88%, 10Y 4.44%, 30Y 5.00%, [Fed H15 via OpenBB](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/)) left room for relief favouring his big-ticket/housing Outperform names; the S&P 500 rose **+12.4%** from 5,604.14 (2025-05-01) to 6,296.79 (2025-07-18), so markets already discounted severe damage ([OpenBB/Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/history/)).

## Limitations

Finnhub company news for TGT and BBY (2025-05-01 → 2025-07-21) returned no records — a coverage gap, not absence of news. No pre-cutoff source states Feldman's post-cut EPS numbers for Best Buy, Walmart or Costco (only his $1.72 pre-print Target estimate), so "EPS cuts" is documented for Target estimates and company guidance, and inferred elsewhere from price-target reductions. OpenBB data are retrospective observations, not frozen vintages. No pre-cutoff document contains Feldman using the word "bifurcation"; that framing is my inference. question: How effectively can Mercedes-Benz Group (MBGYY) mitigate the impact of declining U.S. EV sales and potential trade tariffs through its strategic consolidation of North American operations, aggressive budget cuts, and the proposed shift in production toward its Alabama manufacturing facility?
report:
# Mercedes-Benz Group (MBGYY): Can localisation, consolidation and cost cuts offset U.S. EV weakness and tariffs?

**Point-in-time cutoff: 2025-08-05. All evidence below was published on or before that date.**

## Direct answer

Partially, and with a two-year timing gap. Based on disclosed evidence, Mercedes-Benz Group's three levers address **different, only partly overlapping** problems:

- **Alabama localisation** is the only lever that structurally attacks the tariff, but the announced GLC build starts **late 2027**, so it cannot mitigate 2025–2026 tariff drag ([Automotive Manufacturing Solutions, 2025-05-13](https://www.automotivemanufacturingsolutions.com/oems/mercedes-benz-to-localise-glc-suv-production-in-alabama-amid-tariff-pressures-and-market-shifts/534249)).
- **North American consolidation** into Sandy Springs/Atlanta is an SG&A and speed-to-market measure with **no disclosed savings figure**, so its earnings contribution cannot be verified ([Georgia Governor's Office, 2025-05-22](https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2025-05-22/gov-kemp-mercedes-benz-establishing-north-american-headquarters-new); [WardsAuto, 2025-05-30](https://www.wardsauto.com/news/archive-auto-mercedes-benz-atlanta-north-american-hq/749054)).
- **Budget cuts** (the group-wide "Next Level Performance" programme) are real and large (≈€5bn by 2027), but they are concentrated in German administration/management and China overheads, i.e. they repair the **cost base**, not the **tariff cost line** ([CBT News, 2025-03-04](https://www.cbtnews.com/mercedes-benz-implements-cost-cutting-measures-amid-economic-pressures); [Reuters, 2025-02-27](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/mercedes-benz-plans-cut-15-jobs-china-bloomberg-news-reports-2025-02-27)).

The declining U.S. EV business is, by contrast, the **smallest** of the three exposures: battery-electric cars were 75,700 of ~900,000 group car sales in H1 2025 (**8.4%**, computed from reported volumes), so withdrawing from it protects margin but forfeits future volume rather than saving the current P&L ([Mercedes-Benz Group Q2 2025 interim release, 2025-07-30](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025); [MercedesBlog sales compilation, 2025-07-09](https://mercedesblog.com/crisis-at-mercedes-declining-mercedes-sales-across-all-segments-in-q2-2025)).

## Facts: what is actually documented

**Tariff shock (largest quantified exposure).** U.S. Section 232 levies of 25% on imported vehicles took effect April 2025, with EU-built cars facing a 27.5% rate including parts ([CNBC, 2025-05-01](https://www.cnbc.com/2025-05-01/mercedes-benz-alabama-plant-trump-tariffs.html); [Reuters, 2025-07-28](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-eu-avert-trade-war-with-15-tariff-deal-2025-07-28)). Mercedes reported a **€370m tariff impact in Q2 2025 alone, cutting the EBIT margin by ~1.5 percentage points** ([New Mobility, 2025-07-31](https://newmobility.news/en/2025-07-31/us-tariffs-hurt-mercedes-porsche-and-audi-most-among-german-carmakers)). This triangulates with the company's own disclosure: Mercedes-Benz Cars' Q2 margin was **5.1% adjusted, versus 6.6% "excluding the latest additional tariffs"** — the same 1.5pp gap ([Mercedes-Benz Group, 2025-07-30](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025)). Annualising €370m gives **€1.48bn ≈ $1.7bn** at an assumed 1.15 USD/EUR, which coincides with the press estimate of **"$1.7bn additional costs"** attributed to the tariffs ([AMS, 2025-05-13](https://www.automotivemanufacturingsolutions.com/oems/mercedes-benz-to-localise-glc-suv-production-in-alabama-amid-tariff-pressures-and-market-shifts/534249)). *Assumption, not retrieved data: the 1.15 FX rate and the straight-line annualisation.* Group Q2 EBIT fell **68% to €1.27bn** (adjusted €2.0bn vs €4.0bn), revenue was **€33.2bn (−10%)**, while industrial free cash flow rose to **€1.9bn (H1: €4.2bn)** and net liquidity reached **€30.8bn** ([Investing.com Q2 slide analysis, 2025-07-30](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/mercedesbenz-q2-2025-slides-profit-plunges-68-as-tariffs-and-china-headwinds-bite-93CH-4158873); [Mercedes-Benz Group, 2025-07-30](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025)). Guidance was **pulled at the end of April** because of tariff uncertainty ([Reuters, 2025-05-01](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/mercedes-details-plans-us-production-investments-alabama-2025-05-01); [NYT, 2025-04-30](https://www.nytimes.com/2025-04-30/business/european-automakers-tariff-uncertainty.html)).

**U.S. EV decline.** U.S. Mercedes EV sales fell **more than 50% in H1 2025** per Cox Automotive data ([InsideEVs, 2025-07-18](https://insideevs.com/news/766274/ev-sales-us-q2-winners)), against a U.S. market where Q2 EV sales fell ~6% — only the third annual decline on record. The company cut EQ prices by **$4,410 (EQS sedan) to $15,300 (EQS SUV)** for MY2026 and **paused U.S.-market EQ production/sales from 1 September 2025**, ahead of the Sept-30 expiry of the $7,500 federal credit, with **no restart date** ([Car and Driver, 2025-07-18, updated 2025-07-20](https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a65450365/mercedes-cuts-eq-pricing-ends-us-production)).

**Localisation.** Mercedes first flagged an unnamed "core segment" vehicle for Tuscaloosa by 2027 (1 May), then confirmed the **GLC** — its U.S. best-seller at **64,163 units, ~20% of U.S. car volume** — from late 2027, with AutoForecast projecting **>50,000 units** in the first full year. No physical expansion is needed; the plant runs at **87% of 305,000 capacity**, employs ~11,000 in the U.S. with 400+ suppliers, and exports ~60% of its SUVs ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025-05-01/mercedes-benz-alabama-plant-trump-tariffs.html); [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/mercedes-details-plans-us-production-investments-alabama-2025-05-01); [AMS, 2025-05-13](https://www.automotivemanufacturingsolutions.com/oems/mercedes-benz-to-localise-glc-suv-production-in-alabama-amid-tariff-pressures-and-market-shifts/534249)).

**Cost discipline.** Works-council agreement on voluntary buyouts and **halved salary increases**, with job guarantees to 2034; severance up to €500,000 for long-serving managers; **10–15% cuts in China sales/finance roles**; and Q2 group EBIT absorbing **€715m of adjustments** "mainly for measures to increase operational efficiency" plus M&A, including the sale of Argentine production/sales capacity ([CBT News](https://www.cbtnews.com/mercedes-benz-implements-cost-cutting-measures-amid-economic-pressures); [it-daily.net, 2025-03-21](https://www.it-daily.net/shortnews-en/mercedes-benz-up-to-500000-euros-for-voluntary-job-cancellation); [Reuters, 2025-02-27](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/mercedes-benz-plans-cut-15-jobs-china-bloomberg-news-reports-2025-02-27); [Mercedes-Benz Group, 2025-07-30](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025)).

## Mechanisms (inference)

1. **Tariff-base erosion.** U.S. assembly removes finished-vehicle duty on localised volume. Illustrative scenario: 50,000 GLCs at an assumed $50,000 MSRP, ~80% import-equivalent content and a 15-point tariff differential ⇒ **≈$300m/year of avoided duty** — roughly one-fifth of the $1.7bn exposure, from one model line (my assumptions, not company guidance).
2. **Volume/mix substitution instead of price cuts.** Group sales in North America fell **14% to 80,600** in Q2 while **deliveries to customers rose 26%** in the U.S. — i.e. Mercedes throttled wholesale to defend net pricing, a deliberate shock absorber against tariff pass-through ([Mercedes-Benz USA release, 2025-07-08](https://media.mbusa.com/releases/mercedes-benz-sold-547100-cars-and-vans-in-q2); [Mercedes-Benz Group, 2025-07-30](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025)).
3. **EQ pause is a margin-defence, not a strategy reversal.** PHEV demand rose **34%** in Q2 and xEV **+4%**, so hybrids absorb the displaced EV demand while Top-End stays at 14.3% of sales ([Mercedes-Benz Group, 2025-07-30](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025)).
4. **Trade policy partly solves the problem for them.** The 27 July U.S.–EU framework set a **15% baseline from 1 August**, halving the threatened 27.5%/30% scenario ([Reuters, 2025-07-28](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-eu-avert-trade-war-with-15-tariff-deal-2025-07-28); [DW, 2025-07-27/28](https://www.dw.com/en/eu-us-trade-deal-european-leaders-back-plan-amid-criticism/live-73432200); [Car and Driver, 2025-07-29](https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a65542782/us-european-union-trade-deal-car-tariffs)). U.S. parts-offset relief (3.75% of MSRP for 2025–26) also lowers the localisation premium ([Fox Business, 2025-05-01](https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/trump-eases-auto-tariffs-mercedes-expand-alabama-plant)).

## Counterarguments and risks

- **Time-to-effect mismatch.** The 1.5pp quarterly margin drag is immediate; GLC localisation arrives ~2.5 years later. Tariff relief cuts the *future* prize: if the rate is already 15%, avoided duty shrinks proportionally and localisation economics weaken.
- **Capacity displacement.** At 87% utilisation and 60% export share, adding ~50,000 GLCs is largely a **reallocation of the export base**, not incremental U.S. supply; it reduces EU→U.S. duty but also raises questions about European plants (Bremen loses the GLC line).
- **Cost cuts are not tariff hedges.** ≈€5bn of savings by 2027 is spread group-wide; the €1.48bn annualised tariff run-rate alone is ~30% of that. Union protections (no compulsory redundancy; guarantee to 2034) cap how fast German/European overhead can fall ([CBT News](https://www.cbtnews.com/mercedes-benz-implements-cost-cutting-measures-amid-economic-pressures)).
- **Bigger problem sits in China, not the U.S.** Asia volumes fell **16%**, China **19%**, in Q2 — demand and competitive losses there are not addressed by any North American lever ([MercedesBlog, 2025-07-09](https://mercedesblog.com/crisis-at-mercedes-declining-mercedes-sales-across-all-segments-in-q2-2025)).
- **Optionality cost.** Abandoning the U.S. BEV segment before the credit cliff may preserve near-term margin but cedes the entry-EV customer to Tesla/BYD-adjacent rivals; the new CLA and electric G-Class were the products expected to re-engage them ([InsideEVs, 2025-07-18](https://insideevs.com/news/766274/ev-sales-us-q2-winners)).

## Scenarios (clearly labelled, not forecasts)

| **Base** | 15% EU tariff holds from 1 Aug 2025; GLC ramps late 2027; cost programme delivers ≈€5bn by 2027 | Tariff drag roughly halves vs 27.5%; localisation adds ≈$0.3bn/yr gross relief from 2028 ⇒ U.S. exposure **manageable but not neutralised** by 2026 |
| **Adverse** | Tariff re-escalation/parts levies; U.S. luxury demand softens after credit expiry; savings slip | Adjusted Cars margin stays ≤5%; €1.5bn+ annual EBIT drag exceeds NA-specific savings ⇒ mitigation **fails on timing** |
| **Favourable** | Deeper localisation (more models, van assembly in Charleston), strong Top-End/PHEV mix, Atlanta consolidation lifts SG&A | RoS recovers toward the ex-tariff 6.6%+; U.S. becomes a **hedge**, not a drag |

## Evidence gaps and limitations

Finnhub company news for **MBGYY returned zero admitted results** for 2025-05-01→2025-08-05, so no market-price, ADR-quote or insider-filing evidence was obtained, and no OpenBB index/FX/yield series was retrieved; the USD/EUR rate above is an explicit assumption.
